subject: Re: OpsLyft discovery — latency & context window follow-up
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@opslyft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20 10:15 PST
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets & context window (OpsLyft discovery)

Rajesh — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap of what I heard and actions we agreed: 

- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile tail needs to be <= 250ms for start-of-stream (first byte) and <= 1.25s for < 512-token responses. For longer outputs (512–1,024 tokens) aim for P95 <= 1.8s.
- Concurrency: target sustained concurrent sessions of ~200 (peaks to 350) across your EU+US user base; routing by region required.
- Throughput/TPM: estimated steady-state 6k tokens/minute during peak ramp (mixed input lengths).
- Streaming: partial token delivery required (progressive JSON chunks); server-side streaming preferred to reduce perceived latency.
- Context window: typical user messages include ~3.5k input tokens, but some workflows attach long documents — up to ~24k tokens input in rare cases. You requested the ability to accept up to 32k when required but have fallback options if SLOs degrade.

Next steps I committed to: 
1) Share a short SLO-impact matrix (attached spreadsheet) showing expected P95 vs. output token size across our recommended model variants and quantization levels.
2) Provide a proposed fallback routing policy: prefer fast quantized model for streaming; if latency > 300ms for first byte we fallback to smaller-context variant and send a user-facing note.
3) Schedule an ops sizing follow-up this week for a throughput check (Ben).

Attachments: opslyft_slo_requirements.xlsx (SLO matrix draft), call recording (mp3).

Thanks — Prio
--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai

From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@opslyft.com>

Cc: opslyft-sales@opslyft.com
Date: 2026-12-20 12:03 PST
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & context window (OpsLyft discovery)

Thanks Prio — that's accurate. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 32k input need is gated: only for "document ingestion" flows (~5% of requests) where the customer uploads long logs. For those we can accept higher completion latency if we surface progressive results.
- For our chat UX we need streaming of partial completions at a minimum every ~150ms so the UI can animate. If the model cannot produce token sub-chunks that fast, we prefer small-chunk streaming (every 300ms) over a full non-streamed response.
- Security: the documents are PII-lite, but we need audit logs for requests and model version pinned during the POC.

Can Ben share a brief note on how Redwood would both meet the 150–300ms streaming cadence and how batching might impact that? Also please include suggested default model variant and a fallback timeline.

— Rajesh

Subject: OpsLyft sizing request — P95 streaming cadence & batching constraints

Ben — looping you in. Rajesh called out an aggressive streaming cadence (150ms partials ideally), 200 sustained concurrency, spikes to 350, and a small % of 32k inputs. Can you confirm: 

1) Which model families can realistically deliver first-byte streaming sub-200ms for small inputs (<=1k tokens) on our Dedicated pools?
2) What's the expected P95 for long outputs (>512 tokens) under continuous batching at 100 qps vs. 300 qps?
3) For the 32k inputs, recommend: a) allow them on the same route (with circuit-breaker at 500ms first-byte) or b) route to a heavy-process async job and stream partials from an incremental indexer.

I attached the SLO matrix — please annotate and return by EOD tomorrow so we can update the OpsLyft doc and send a tight proposal.

thanks,
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@opslyft.com>
Date: 2026-12-21 09:22 PST
Subject: Re: OpsLyft sizing request — P95 streaming cadence & batching constraints

Marissa / Prio / Rajesh — quick technical readout and proposed ops plan: 

TL;DR: We can meet the streaming cadence & concurrency goals with the following combination: a low-latency quantized variant for chat (primary), a larger-context async path for 32k uploads, and an adaptive fallback that trades off output length for latency.

Details: 
- Small-input streaming (<=1k tokens): On Dedicated A100-style pools using our ~8-bit quantized chat variant (q8b-chat-1), we expect median first-byte ~60–90ms and P95 ~180–240ms at up to 250 concurrent streaming sessions with continuous batching disabled for those routes. If you enable small-window batching (2–4 reqs), P95 may shift +30–70ms depending on request alignment.

- Mid-length outputs (512–1k tokens): With streaming enabled, total completion P95 is dominated by token emission; we project P95 ~1.3–1.6s at 200 sustained concurrency. At 300 qps high-batching conditions (batching window 20ms), P95 could increase to ~2.0s unless we reduce batch size or reserve capacity.

- 32k inputs (document ingestion): Recommend routing to a separate async path: accept upload, run incremental chunking + local KV cache, and stream back incremental summaries. This keeps realtime chat unaffected. If you must serve same-route, expect significant P95 tail (>4s) for completions and potential violations of the 250ms first-byte SLO.

- Fallbacks & policies: 
  * Policy A (preferred): Primary route -> q8b-chat-1 (streaming); if first-byte latency > 300ms for 3 consecutive requests, circuit-break to q4b-fast variant (reduced context) and append user-facing banner "Using condensed context to improve latency".
  * Policy B (async for large inputs): 32k uploads -> async ingestion route + incremental stream; provide webhook/WS callback.

- Observability + audit: We'll enable request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns during POC and retain audit logs for 90 days (longer via add-on).

Next actions: 
1) Prio: send OpsLyft the annotated SLO matrix (I added in-sheet notes).
2) Marissa: propose a Dedicated pool size (GPU count) — I estimate 8 x A100-equivalent for baseline with autoscale to 12 for peaks.
3) Rajesh: confirm whether 32k uploads must be realtime or can go async for the POC.

If you prefer, we can run a short bench: 2-hour soak with representative traces (we'll need a sample dataset). I can prep a runbook for the soak.

Ben
